stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: Messi nets 100th Miami goal en route to Campeones Cup win
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in all competitions after heading home the opener in a 2-0 win over Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Lionel Messi scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in all competitions after heading home the opener in a 2-0 win over Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.

Messi's goal put Miami up 1-0 in the annual match between the champion of MLS and Liga MX before a late header from Casemiro put the game away to hand new coach Cristian "Kily" González a trophy in his first match in charge.

"Leo [Messi] told me I was going to become a champion, and he made it happen," González said.

"Moving forward, this gives us a huge morale boost, it's a vital element for us, and while we've achieved this, we have to keep going."

Luis Suárez set up the opener in the 24th minute with a perfectly lofted cross from the right side that Messi ran onto, outjumping his marker and scoring a rare goal with his head.

González led his first training session with Inter Miami on Tuesday after landing in Miami from Argentina earlier in the morning. The team had reached an agreement with González to replace interim coach Guillermo Hoyos on Aug. 27, but he was unable to take over until receiving his work permit.

His first game as Miami coach will be one to remember with Messi scoring his 100th goal for the club and the team picking up a trophy on the night.

"It's become a normality [for Messi] but it isn't," Rodrigo de Paul said about his Miami teammate.

"We have to enjoy him, admire him, see him with the love that he plays each game. Luckily, I've had him by my side for many years. I try to enjoy him to the maximum."

Messi, a World Cup winner in 2022, reached the milestone in only 115 games for Inter Miami, marking the quickest he has recorded 100 goals for any team he has represented. Messi previously reached the mark with Barcelona in 188 games and 174 games with Argentina.

Since joining Miami in 2023, Messi has 76 goals in MLS, 14 in Leagues Cup action, eight in the Concacaf Champions Cup and one at the FIFA Club World Cup.

Messi made an instant impact in south Florida since signing with Miami, leading the Herons to the 2023 Leagues Cup title just weeks after marking his debut against Cruz Azul -- the team against which he scored his first Miami goal.

The Inter Miami captain also guided the team to the 2024 Supporters' Shield -- setting the record for most points (74) in an MLS season -- and starred in the playoffs during a run to the 2025 MLS Cup title last year.

Messi has now scored 929 goals for club and country during his career and leads MLS with 19 goals in 22 games so far this season.

stories.headline: Toronto Raptors offseason recap, early 2026-27 season preview
stories.summary: With Leonard and Barnes, the Raptors are hoping to bring the franchise back to title contention. Question is: Do they have enough in a stronger East to do it?
stories.body:
The Raptors' road to real Eastern Conference contention opened in earnest Monday, when Toronto and the LA Clippers finally hit send on their long-delayed trade that will send seven-time All-Star Kawhi Leonard to Toronto for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap and two second-round picks.

The trade ends a saga that enveloped both teams, as the NBA completed its nearly year-long investigation into allegations of salary cap circumvention stemming from the Clippers' dealings with Leonard over the course of his tenure in Los Angeles.

Now with Leonard in Toronto, the two-time Finals MVP will pair with rising star Scottie Barnes and second-year big Collin Murray-Boyles, hoping to replicate the success of their title run in 2019.

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the 2026-27 season, with 30 previews -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Friday. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more.

Quick links:

Roster | Depth chart | Transactions

More Raptors coverage | More NBA

Offseason at a glance
Key additions: Kawhi Leonard, Kyle Anderson, Andre Jackson Jr.

Key subtractions: Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, Sandro Mamukelashvili

Key retentions: Jamal Shead

After waiting months to finalize their acquisition of Leonard from the Clippers because of the NBA's investigation into salary cap circumvention, the Raptors can finally look ahead to what could be their most promising season in years.

Leonard, who led Toronto to the 2019 championship, plugs in as a major positional upgrade over Ingram. The rest of the Raptors' starting lineup remains intact, and forward Collin Murray-Boyles should only improve after a standout rookie campaign.

While losing Mamukelashvili in free agency took a bite out of their bench unit, Toronto has crafted a high-energy and versatile supporting cast for Leonard and two-time All-Star Scottie Barnes.

The plucky Raptors, who won 46 games last season, have a real shot to win their first playoff series since 2020. -- Ben Golliver

Zach Kram's offseason grade: A

Toronto's only real move of consequence this summer was trading for Kawhi Leonard, who should bring major improvements over Brandon Ingram on both ends -- especially offense, where Leonard is the sort of primary option and half-court scorer whom the previous version of the Raptors lacked.

The cost in draft picks was substantially greater than the last time Toronto traded for Leonard, eight years ago, but it was a worthwhile risk for a team that now has a legitimate chance to reach the Finals if Leonard can stay healthy next season. That gamble worked out eight years ago, after all. -- Kram

What we learned this offseason
The Raptors had two good reasons to go through with the Kawhi Leonard trade.

After enjoying a 16-win jump in the standings and snapping a three-year playoff drought, the Raptors entered the summer with a bunch of big contracts on their books and limited avenues to take the next step.

The simplest path to improvement involved packaging either Immanuel Quickley or Brandon Ingram along with other players or picks for positional upgrades. Given the hearty salaries owed to Quickley and Ingram, that wasn't going to be an easy task. But the Raptors managed to construct exactly this type of trade by sending Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks, a first-round swap and two second-round picks to the LA Clippers for Kawhi Leonard.

The primary goal of the deal, of course, was to bring Leonard back to the organization he led to the 2019 title. With a two-time Finals MVP in place, Toronto could feel much more comfortable against the East's elite and start dreaming about winning its first playoff series since 2020.

The trade's other huge benefit was shedding Ingram's contract. The two-time All-Star disappeared during the 2026 playoffs, and he is owed $40 million in 2026-27 and $41.9 million in 2027-28.

While trading for Ingram in 2025 and subsequently re-signing him were both ill-advised decisions, flipping him for Leonard amounted to a brilliant use of the undo button.

The long-discussed Leonard trade was finally consummated Monday after the NBA completed its investigation into allegations of salary cap circumvention. Once the league office announced that Leonard's punishment was limited to a $700,000 fine, Toronto was able to proceed with a bold move that added talent and fixed a past mistake. -- Golliver

The big question: How high is Scottie Barnes' ceiling?
Barnes' impressive growth shouldn't get lost in all the hubbub over Leonard's arrival.

The 2021 lottery pick really came into his own during his age-24 season, improving his scoring efficiency, earning his first All-Defensive Team selection and raising his game against the Cleveland Cavaliers in the playoffs.

While the Raptors lost their first-round series in seven games, Barnes averaged 24.1 points, 6.1 rebounds, 8.6 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.7 blocks per game -- a level of all-around playoff production matched only by LeBron James, Nikola Jokic and Cade Cunningham over the past decade.

Barnes should be regarded as one of the leading Defensive Player of the Year candidates, and he just might pop up on future MVP ballots if his upward trajectory and Toronto's winning ways continue. -- Golliver

Basketball Power Index rank: No. 14
Here are the predicted net points per 100 possessions for the Raptors' top seven players for the 2026-27 season:

Kawhi Leonard shot 6.8 3-pointers per game last year, a career high, at 39%, below what he shot in each of the four prior seasons. But the extra volume meant he added plus-1.9 net points per 100 possessions on 3s vs. plus-1.6 in prior years. That's not a huge bump, but it's relevant.

Also, Leonard is one of those rare players whose college 3-point percentage was really low (25%), only to shoot really well in the NBA (39%). -- Dean Oliver

Read about how net points works here.

Biggest X factor this season
PF Collin Murray-Boyles

Ever since the Raptors agreed to acquire Leonard from the Clippers, thoughts of the Leonard/Barnes/Murray-Boyles defensive trio have tantalized. That's the key group and lineup combination that could propel the Raptors to lofty heights this season.

So even though Murray-Boyles is only a second-year player who averaged 8.5 points as a rookie, he profiles as one of the biggest X factors in the league.

For the Raptors to maximize their window with Leonard, they need Murray-Boyles to take greater steps this season and prove his bona fides as a small-ball center who can replace Jakob Poeltl in clutch situations. -- Kram

stories.headline: UFC 331 preview and picks: Pantoja sees opportunity in disaster
stories.summary: Top storylines and coaches' analysis for UFC 331 in Los Angeles.
stories.body:
For two and a half years, Alexandre Pantoja ruled the UFC's flyweight division at a level unseen since the historic era of Demetrious Johnson nearly 10 years ago. And yet, the past nine months since his last fight could prove to be the most compelling of Pantoja's career.
The 36-year-old Pantoja (30-6) will challenge Joshua Van (17-2) for the 125-pound championship at UFC 331 inside Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Saturday. It will be his first appearance since UFC 323 in December, when he lost the belt to Van via TKO after Pantoja suffered a dislocated elbow 26 seconds into the fight. The nature of the loss has led to a feeling of unfinished business between the two fighters going into Saturday's main event.

"As an athlete, yes, I have a TKO loss on my record," Pantoja told ESPN. "I've never lost by TKO or submission before. Nobody had ever finished me. Now, I have that. But personally, as a man? No. I don't believe I have a loss to him."

Pantoja won the title against Brandon Moreno in 2023 and defended the belt four times before meeting Van. He was among the best pound-for-pound fighters in the world at the time. But with a comeback narrative attached to him for this fight, he said there is an added level of excitement.

"For sure, this is an opportunity," Pantoja said. "In my soul, that's the opportunity. Now, I get to fight the champion. He's the champion of the world and I love that. It makes the fight more spicy for me."

Van, 24, has embraced the narrative -- even while cementing himself as the undisputed champion. There are those who say Van needs to defeat Pantoja again to legitimize his championship, but Van's first title defense against Tatsuro Taira in May made discrediting him harder. Taira's ground game posed a real threat to Van, but he ultimately knocked out the Japanese challenger in the fifth round of a matchup that earned fight of the night honors at UFC 328.

The unfinished business, Pantoja's return and Van's undeniable star power mean Saturday's flyweight title fight is shaping up to be the most anticipated 125-pound title fight since Henry Cejudo ended Johnson's nearly five-year title reign in 2018 then defended the flyweight belt against then-bantamweight champion TJ Dillashaw in 2019.

For Pantoja specifically, his worst stroke of bad luck could turn into the greatest night of his career.

"Saturday night is going to be my best night, man," Pantoja said. "I haven't been to work in 10 months. That's why all of these fights, and this one especially, is worth so much. We work for months to just get one night of work. I've recovered my arm. Now I have an opportunity to show everyone what I did in the last 10 months."

More storylines to watch
History isn't in Pantoja's favor
If Alexandre Pantoja is searching for role models to inspire this weekend's quest to reclaim the championship he lost suddenly and painfully last December, he would be wise to look beyond recent history.

Within the past two weeks, two of the UFC's 11 champs -- women's flyweight Valentina Shevchenko and heavyweight Tom Aspinall -- vacated their titles because of health issues. Their paths back to the top of the mountain are as yet uncharted.

Before them, the most recent champions to lose their titles to injuries did not fare well upon their returns. In November 2022, Jiří Procházka vacated the UFC light heavyweight title after hurting his shoulder in training. His successor was Jamahal Hill, who just months after winning the vacant title had to vacate it himself after rupturing an Achilles. As soon as he was healed, Hill was granted an opportunity to reclaim his title and lost. Procházka was given three shots at the 205-pound belt and fell short in all of them.

For a success story, Pantoja must look deeper into UFC championship history to the brutal health issues overcome by Dominick Cruz. While preparing for a bantamweight title defense in May 2012, Cruz tore the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee. He underwent surgery, then had a setback requiring a second ACL surgery six months later. He was scheduled to return in February 2014 but suffered a groin tear in training. Facing another extended recovery, he vacated his title.

Cruz returned that September and won a fight that put him in position for a shot at his old belt. Three months later, he tore his other ACL.

Finally, in February 2016 -- more than four years after his last title fight -- Cruz challenged TJ Dillashaw for the belt and won a split decision. "I had to show something to myself," Cruz said afterward. "That's what this was."

Tsarukyan's chance to set things right again
Arman Tsarukyan was labeled a snubbed man after it was announced that Justin Gaethje and Paddy Pimblett would headline the first UFC card of 2026 with the No. 1 lightweight contender status at stake. It's hard to remember that sentiment now, considering the year Tsarukyan has had.

In the absence of an obvious UFC fight to take, Tsarukyan has wrestled competitively -- mostly in RAF -- 10 times in 2026. He raised his social media presence exponentially behind videos of lavish cars, extraordinary meals and collaborations with content creator Nina Drama. This is the longest layoff of his UFC career, but his brand has grown more during that time off than from any single fight.

He appears in a good position to get back to work and finally earn the title shot many have said he should have already had. But it won't be an easy fight. Tsarukyan's opponent, Mauricio Ruffy, is a dangerous underdog (+260, according to DraftKings). This fight will restore the order the top of the 155-pound division has lacked in Tsarukyan's absence, regardless of who wins.

Another step for Steveson?

Any MMA prospect would almost certainly switch places with 26-year-old UFC newcomer Gable Steveson. When you're an Olympic gold medal wrestler, and one of the most touted heavyweight prospects in MMA history, certain opportunities are going to come to you that others aren't afforded. It also means Steveson's window for error is small, as he's asked to learn and develop under the sport's brightest lights.

The UFC is managing his opposition. For his second UFC appearance (and fifth pro fight overall), he'll take on Sean Sharaf, a 33-year-old with two knockout losses in his first two UFC fights. Steveson will once again be a heavy, heavy favorite (-1800 by DraftKings), as he was for his promotional debut in July. The heavyweight division is wide open now that Tom Aspinall has vacated his title and the list of top contenders is thin, so Steveson's performance probably means more than the result. If he continues to look the part, his career trajectory could be accelerated at a rate few see.

Coaches' questions and predictions
"Can Pantoja bank enough rounds on the ground, while staying responsible on the feet?"

What a fight this will be. Van shows up in big moments; he's just a proven gamer. If Pantoja stands with Van, he's going to get hurt. Pantoja is good at applying pressure and landing the 1-2 punch (lead left jab, right cross), but he cannot play that game with Van, because of Van's counterboxing. Van's hands are too fast. Van can land four-to-six shots at a time in close distance, and that's something Pantoja really has to watch for. Van is going to have confidence in his ability to get off the ground from his last fight against Taira. I'm going to stay on the fence and say it's a pick 'em. After watching Van's fight with Taira, though, knowing how good Taira is on the ground, it's a little unfair to say Van can't weather the storm on the ground with Pantoja. -- Sayif Saud, Fortis MMA

Prediction: Too close to call

"How big of a setback is Pantoja's injury at age 36?"
Van is young, fired up and he's got bricks in his hands. We've seen some small weaknesses in his game, which are obviously due to lack of experience. He's getting better all the time. If Pantoja comes back and is anywhere close to where he was when he was holding the belt, I think he gets it back. There are just too many variables on the ground. We saw Van get mounted by Taira. Van is going to go to work on fixing that hole in his game, but Pantoja is so good. The biggest question is how bad of a setback is Pantoja's injury, at this stage of his career? He's not a spring chicken. But if he's the same Pantoja, he gets the win, potentially by submission. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Prediction: Pantoja by decision or submission

"Can Ruffy stop takedowns and keep space?"

Arman has been on such a tear with the wrestling in RAF, showing his ability to wrestle bigger guys and show his power and skill in grappling. When it comes to that, he is very dangerous. Ruffy is finding his groove, and he's very sharp on the feet, but former opponents King Green and Michael Chandler don't pose the same grappling threat that Arman poses. I think Benoît Saint Denis kind of exposed that hole in Ruffy's game. It's not to say Ruffy doesn't have a chance. In space, he is a problem. He can absolutely starch Arman in space. But how does he keep a powerhouse like Arman at distance? -- Saud

Prediction: Tsarukyan by decision

"Has Ruffy improved his ground defense enough?"
This is a really interesting fight. Arman is going to want to grind out Ruffy. Arman is easily a top-five wrestler/grappler in the UFC. The one thing about Arman -- even though he's stayed busy with the wrestling appearances, he's been out of the UFC for a while, so it'll be interesting to see how he looks. But unless Ruffy catches him and knocks him out, Arman is a good striker, too. Arman can go the distance in a hard fight. My gut leans to Arman. I'm a big fan of Ruffy, but it's just that grappling prowess of Arman. -- Wood

Prediction: Tsarukyan by decision

stories.headline: Lando Norris backs 'exciting' 2027 Monaco GP sprint weekend but 'tougher for us drivers'
stories.summary: Lando Norris has backed the decision to make the Monaco Grand Prix a sprint event, saying it should make the event more entertaining for fans.
stories.body:
Lando Norris has backed the decision to make the Monaco Grand Prix a sprint event, saying it should make the event more entertaining for fans.

Monaco's iconic F1 race around its narrow streets has drawn criticism in recent years as a spectacle lacking overtaking and entertainment.

F1's newly released calendar for next year listed the street race as a sprint race -- which means an extra qualifying session to set the grid for a short race, ahead of qualifying for the grand prix itself.

"Interesting," was reigning champion Norris' verdict when asked by Sky Sports about his thoughts at Wentworth's BMW PGA Championship Pro-Am.

The addition of the two competitive sessions comes in place of two practice sessions -- meaning drivers will only have an hour on track to prepare for the weekend.

"I guess the main thing is that means you've got FP1, [sprint] qualifying on Friday -- which is the challenge," the McLaren driver said.

"Obviously not a lot happens in a race on Sunday or in the sprint, but the challenge is just one practice session straight in, which has probably never happened before in Monaco.

- Max vs 100: Verstappen jokes taking on '200' drivers next time after winning crazy challenge

- Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters in 35 minutes

stories.summary: The final edition of weekly picks take you from the WNBA's return to the end of the fantasy women's hoops finals.
stories.body:
The daily news and notes around the WNBA have actionable value when applied to fantasy women's basketball. From lineup changes to hot streaks to injury news, check this page regularly for updates from ESPN's fantasy analysts Eric Moody and André Snellings.

Resources: Rankings | Scoring leaders | Added/dropped | ESPN Fantasy app

Sept. 17: Four players to target in free agency

Andre Snellings: The FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup has concluded, with Team USA staging a massive comeback in the championship game to bring home the gold. The tournament caused a break in the WNBA season right in the middle of the fantasy playoffs, but the break ends on Thursday when the season resumes... with the WNBA at an interesting junction.

All eight playoffs teams are already clinched, but there is plenty of room for teams to move up and down in the standings. In addition, teams will want to enter the postseason on a high note so they will need to play themselves back into form after the layoff. In addition, many of the player contracts signed after last offseason's Collective Bargaining Agreement were for a single year, so a large chunk of the league are effectively in contract years. So, even if a player's team may be out of the playoffs hunt, they may still have quite a bit to play for going into the offseason.

As always, we help you keep your team operating at its best by pointing out some players that may be available on your free agency wire that are performing well enough to be worthy of rostering or streaming.

Sydney Taylor, G, Chicago Sky (Rostered in 34.5% of ESPN Leagues): Taylor was one of the hotter scorers in the WNBA for most of the month of July, when she averaged 19.3 PPG during a 10-game stretch from July 7 through Aug. 1 before injuries slowed her down. She returned from a five-game absence for the end of August but was playing more limited minutes. The layoff gave her time to get healthier for the end of the season which could allow her to finish on another upswing.

Awa Fam, C, Seattle Storm (46.4%): With Ezi Magbegor (knee) out for the season, Fam may be asked to take a larger role for the Storm moving forward. The 20-year-old rookie has had some strong performances in her rookie season and has nightly double-double potential when getting near-starter minutes.

Awak Kuier, C, Dallas Wings (35.4%): Kuier has started six of the last seven games for the Wings with an expanded role since Azzi Fudd went down for the season. Kuier is one of the best shot-blockers and defenders in the league, averaging 3.3 BPG and 1.0 SPG along with a near double-double of 8.7 PPG and 7.4 RPG during that seven game stretch.

Lexi Held, G, Phoenix Mercury (1.4%): Held got a spot start in place of Kahleah Copper in the game before the break and turned in 11 points with three steals and three 3-pointers in 21 minutes. With both Kelsey Plum (leg) and Jovana Nogic (overseas commitment) out for the season, Held is likely to remain a starter for the remainder of the campaign and continue to be a solid source of scoring and 3-point shooting.

2026 fantasy women's basketball awards

Eric Moody: The 2026 season had everything fantasy managers could ask for, with stars delivering on expectations, breakout players and plenty of help from the waiver wire. With the fantasy season almost over, here are my awards for the players who made the biggest impact.

Fantasy MVP: A'ja Wilson, F/C, Las Vegas Aces

Wilson was the safest player in fantasy and once again delivered elite production across the board. She scored, rebounded, blocked shots and created steals at a level few players could match. Wilson ranks first in total fantasy points and fantasy points per game by a significant margin. If you drafted her at 1.01, she lived up to expectations.

Best scorer award for most fantasy points from points and 3-pointers: Kelsey Mitchell, G, Indiana Fever

Mitchell was one of the league's best sources of scoring and 3-pointers all season. She ranked third in 3-pointers per game while shooting 45.5% from beyond the arc, second in points per game and second in field goal attempts per game. Mitchell ranks fifth in total fantasy points largely because of that scoring production, making her a great return on her average draft position.

Box score award for most fantasy points from rebounds, assists, steals and blocks: Angel Reese, F/C, Atlanta Dream

Reese hasn't had to be a prolific scorer to help fantasy managers. Most of her value comes from everything else. She currently holds the single-season rebounding record, passing A'ja Wilson's mark of 451 from the 2024 season. Reese leads the league in rebounds per game and ranks third in steals per game. When you add in her points, assists and blocks, she ranks fourth in total fantasy points. Reese has generated more value from the non-scoring categories than any other player.

Matchup winner award for best fantasy week: A'ja Wilson, F/C, Las Vegas Aces

Wilson also delivered one of the best fantasy stretches of the season. From July 28 through Aug. 1, she scored 166 fantasy points across three games, including 28 points and 14 rebounds, 33 points with 10 rebounds and six assists, and 36 points with 12 rebounds. A week like that can swing an entire fantasy matchup.

Most underrated award for best player under 50% rostered: Leila Lacan, G, Connecticut Sun

Lacan was one of the better under-the-radar fantasy options this season for a Sun team that was one of the worst in the league. She averaged 23.1 fantasy points in 28.4 minutes per game, and her assists and steals gave her value even when the scoring wasn't there. Despite that production, Lacan remained available in far too many leagues for much of the season.

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail semifinals: Bulldogs move to lock away rising rookie
stories.summary: Ronaldo Mulitalo is determined to honour his departing Sharks teammates, Sione Katoa has opened up about his future at the Cowboys and his finals days at the Sharks, while Nathan Cleary is fighting the clock to be fit for Penrith's prelim.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's semifinal week.

Bulldogs move early to lock down rising forward

The Bulldogs have moved early to lock down rising forward Alekolasimi 'AJ' Jones, with the club's Rookie of the Year agreeing to a two-year contract extension.

ESPN understands Jones, who was already contracted through the 2027 season, has agreed to a new deal that will keep him at Belmore beyond his existing contract.

The move ensures Jones' future is secured before he would have been free to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 from November 1.

Kennedy backs Hynes amid criticism

Will Kennedy believes Nicho Hynes has grown from the criticism that has followed him throughout his career, praising the Sharks star ahead of their semi-final against the Roosters.

"He's learned a lot from all the criticism he gets and he's taken a step forward," Kennedy said. "For me, I just want to get around him because he's my brother and I want to play next to him."

Trindall 'really good' after shoulder scare

Will Kennedy says Braydon Trindall has pulled up well after battling through a shoulder issue in Cronulla's finals win over North Queensland.

Kennedy said Trindall had been "really dialled in on the mental side" of his game and indicated the halfback had told him he was feeling "really good" ahead of the Roosters clash.

Mulitalo relishing 'Marky Mark' rematch

Ronaldo Mulitalo is embracing another blockbuster battle with Roosters star Mark Nawaqanitawase, describing the departing winger as a "generational talent".

Mulitalo said Nawaqanitawase "brings the best out of me" and revealed their on-field rivalry is largely one-sided when it comes to the verbal exchanges.

"He's a gentleman out there... he doesn't really say anything. I think it's more myself," Mulitalo joked. "He knows I'm just going to keep talking, so he just ignores me anyway."

Mulitalo determined to honour departing Sharks

Ronaldo Mulitalo says Cronulla's finals run carries added significance with several longtime teammates set to leave the club at season's end.

Mulitalo said he has played alongside some of the departing Sharks since he was 16 and wants to "honour those boys" with his performance against the Roosters.

"I don't want to let them down and disappoint them, winning the game is the most important part of the week for me."

Katoa reveals Cowboys appeal

Sione Katoa has revealed North Queensland's attacking style was a major attraction behind his move to the Cowboys in 2027.

After helping eliminate his future club from the finals, Katoa told ESPN he "loves the style of footy" they play, describing it as "free footy" and similar to Cronulla's attack.

Katoa emotional over Sharks farewell
He also admitted the reality that every game could be his last for Cronulla is beginning to sink in.

"Tonight might have been the last week, maybe the last game," he told ESPN after scoring a double against North Queensland.

"I'm very happy right now that I get another week with my brothers and play again."

Cleary racing clock for preliminary final

Nathan Cleary is in doubt for Penrith's preliminary final after scans revealed an stress-related bone issue in his foot.

The Panthers will assess and monitor their star halfback over the next fortnight, with their week off providing valuable recovery time.

Cleary has, however, been cleared of any suspension concern after receiving only a Grade 1 Dangerous Contact charge for his incident with Hugo Savala.

stories.body:
Fabian Hürzeler called for humility and continued focus on the basics as Brighton host Arsenal fresh from their remarkable Carabao Cup turnaround at Manchester United.

The Seagulls became the first team since 1976 to overturn a two-goal deficit and win at Old Trafford as substitute Maxim De Cuyper completed a thrilling, and thoroughly deserved, 3-2 comeback win.

Brighton boss Hürzeler said belief was key to Wednesday's turnaround but also that he is not getting ahead of himself as the Premier League champions head to the Amex on Saturday.

"I think that we have to stay very, very humble now and get an understanding why we are in the place where we are," the Albion manager said.

"It's about doing the basic things right and doing the small margins right, and therefore it's so important that we keep this in our mind.

"That we stay humble, that we don't take these things for granted, that we step into the game and understand 'OK, it's hard work again.'

Did you know that four-team fantasy leagues are one of the most popular formats here at ESPN Fantasy Hockey? This small league format allows for star-studded rosters and a high-quality of free agents available at any time.

But it's not all a points-palooza, your opponents all have star-studded lineups as well which bring about a different layer of difficulty. Our fantasy hockey staff -- Sean Allen, Pierre, Becquey, Sachin Chandan and Victoria Matiash -- took part in a mock draft with each one taking different strategy. You can see their comments below, as well as how their teams shaped up.

An indispensable strategy in just about all redraft competition, the art of streaming is even more important in ultra-tight leagues. Just look at some of these characters still available after our four-team draft: Brandon Hagel, Tom Wilson, Vincent Trocheck, Brayden Point, Victor Hedman etc! Considering the glut of very good players both rostered and still available, flipping them in and out weekly, or even daily, to ice the most active bodies possible makes great sense.

Hacking the schedule obviously plays a big part here. Using my own squad as an example, I'm theoretically happy to bid farewell to Kirill Marchenko in exchange for Point, if Columbus is only playing Tuesday and Saturday, while Tampa Bay is in action Monday, Wednesday, Friday, and Sunday (the NHL Fantasy manager's most coveted weekly slate). It's not only about the number of games, but rhythm too. This is a Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday league. Filling a lineup the rest of the week is a greater challenge when fewer teams are in action.

stories.headline: NBA offseason recap, early 2026-27 season previews by team
stories.summary: We're looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the regular season by rolling out one team profile each weekday through Sept. 18.
stories.body:
After an eventful July full of big trades, intriguing signings and the game's biggest star shocking everyone by heading East, the NBA offseason is nearly complete. And with the regular-season schedule now out, it's time to start thinking about the 2026-27 season.

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for every team.

Check out the rollout schedule below, with stories added daily:

Quick links:

Free agency buzz | FA grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Schedule | More NBA coverage

Atlantic Division

Philadelphia 76ers: Sept. 14
Key additions: F LeBron James, G Jaylen Brown, G Anfernee Simons, F Dean Wade, G Labaron Philon Jr., G Kentavious Caldwell-Pope

Key subtractions: F Paul George, C Andre Drummond, G Quentin Grimes, G Kelly Oubre Jr.

No team changed its fortunes from April to July as drastically as the 76ers. Taking advantage of Boston's desire to get out of the Jaylen Brown business enabled it to accomplish so much: getting a motivated All-Star feeling the sting of rejection following a career year, dumping George's contract and putting themselves in position to be attractive to an all-time great in James, who was looking for a new challenge. They also lessened their dependency on Joel Embiid's bothersome health as he will turn 33 during the season.

They filled in the blanks by adding Caldwell-Pope and Wade as plug-and-play wings, changing the complexion of their franchise in several swoops. If nothing else, they won the offseason. -- Vincent Goodwill

Read the full 76ers offseason recap/season preview

Boston Celtics: Sept. 15
Key additions: Paul George, Mitchell Robinson, Mike Conley

Key subtractions: Jaylen Brown, Nikola Vucevic

Key retentions: Neemias Queta, Jordan Walsh, Ron Harper Jr.

Boston responded to its first early playoff exit since 2021 by boldly trading Brown to the 76ers, ending his fruitful partnership with Jayson Tatum. The move should improve the Celtics' long-term flexibility to build around Tatum, but next year's iteration will require the aging George to discover the fountain of youth. The 36-year-old forward has played in 60 games just once in the past seven seasons.

Even so, this shouldn't be viewed as a gap year. The Celtics return a cohesive nucleus, and they added Robinson's defense and rebounding to shore up a frontcourt rotation that was overwhelmed in the postseason.

If Tatum returns to superstar form in his first fully healthy season since a May 2025 Achilles injury, the Celtics will have a chance to win at least 50 games for the sixth straight year. Securing Banner 19, however, will likely require finding a superstar replacement for Brown sometime down the road. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Celtics offseason recap/season preview

Brooklyn Nets: Sept. 16
Key additions: F Julius Randle, G Mikel Brown Jr., G Keon Ellis

Key subtractions: C Nic Claxton

Key retentions: C Day'Ron Sharpe, F Josh Minott

Once commissioner Adam Silver responded to last season's shameless tankathon by nearly a third of the league's teams by implementing a draft lottery reform, the Nets could no longer slow-play their rebuild by hoping for ping-pong luck. Getting Randle back to New York, but this time across town from his former team, and one he watched win an NBA championship without him, was a big move for the Nets. Plus, drafting a promising point guard, Brown at No. 6, in this year's draft adds to a glut of guards on the roster, but the Nets were in serious need of a talent upgrade across the board. Even with the addition of Randle, who's due to make $33.3 million this season, the Nets are still well below the salary cap, meaning they can take in plenty of money in deals should the opportunity present itself. -- Vincent Goodwill

Read the full Nets offseason recap/season preview

Toronto Raptors: Sept. 17
Key additions: Kawhi Leonard, Kyle Anderson, Andre Jackson Jr.

Key subtractions: Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, Sandro Mamukelashvili

Key retentions: Jamal Shead

After waiting months to finalize their acquisition of Leonard from the Clippers due to the NBA's investigation into salary cap circumvention, the Raptors can finally look ahead to what could be their most promising season in years.

Leonard, who led Toronto to the 2019 championship, plugs in as a major positional upgrade over Ingram. The rest of the Raptors' starting lineup remains intact, and forward Collin Murray-Boyles should only improve after a standout rookie campaign.

While losing Mamukelashvili in free agency took a bite out of their bench unit, Toronto has crafted a high-energy and versatile supporting cast for Leonard and two-time All-Star Scottie Barnes.

The plucky Raptors, who won 46 games last season, have a real shot to win their first playoff series since 2020. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Raptors offseason recap/season preview

New York Knicks: Sept. 18

h2>Central Division

Milwaukee Bucks: Sept. 7
Key additions: Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, Caris LeVert

Key retentions: Gary Trent Jr.

Key subtractions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bobby Portis

After 13 seasons, the Giannis era ended in Milwaukee with a mega trade to the Heat -- and the 2026-27 season will mark a major shift for the rebuilding franchise.

The Bucks hired coach Taylor Jenkins to establish a culture. They added four new players from Miami, including former All-Star and Wisconsin native Tyler Herro, and selected Brayden Burries with the No. 10 pick in June.

The Bucks will enter the season with an ill-fitting mix of players and low expectations, but they have the luxury to see what sticks long term. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full Bucks offseason recap/season preview

Chicago Bulls: Sept. 8
Key additions: F Caleb Wilson, G Dailyn Swain, C Nic Claxton, G Norman Powell, Tiago Splitter

Key subtractions: None

Key retentions: F Zach Collins

For years, Chicago has been seen as one of the sleeping giants of the NBA, a once-proud franchise reduced to meandering in the play-in tournament and in the middle of the lottery in recent seasons. But the Bulls got a much-needed makeover this summer and enter the 2026-27 season with a clearer direction than they've had in years.

The changes have been full-scale: Bryson Graham was hired as the team's new head of basketball operations, Tiago Splitter will patrol the sidelines as head coach, No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson is the new face of the franchise, and he'll be surrounded by some veterans like Nic Claxton and Norman Powell to help ease his transition. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full Bulls offseason recap/season preview

Cleveland Cavaliers: Sept. 9
Key additions: Peyton Watson, Mario Hezonja

Key subtractions: Dean Wade, Dennis Schroder, Max Strus, Larry Nance Jr., Caris Levert, Keon Ellis

Key retentions: Donovan Mitchell, James Harden

The Cavs' failed pursuit of LeBron James this summer turned into a pivot for a younger, athletic wing, prying Watson from the Nuggets after a career-year.

Watson averaged career highs in points, rebounds, assists and steals while shooting 41% from 3 last year, and he has in recent years been one of the strongest wing defenders in the league. That makes him a strong complement next to James Harden and Donovan Mitchell, as the Cavs hope he can provide a substantial answer to the elusive fifth starter role next to their core four. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full Cavaliers offseason recap/season preview

Detroit Pistons: Sept. 10
Key additions: John Collins, Isaiah Joe, Taurean Prince, Gary Harris

Key subtractions: Tobias Harris, Isaiah Stewart

Key retentions: None

The Pistons' offseason is still in limbo as negotiations with restricted free agent Jalen Duren have stalled.

Detroit believes it sent Duren a fair offer considering the totality of his 2025-26 season -- including his underwhelming playoff showing -- while Duren feels like he's checked off all the boxes to get more.

Losing Harris and Stewart will be a big test to their culture -- or a signal they have to win a different way than in the last two seasons.

They added shooting on the margins with Joe, Prince and Harris. And assuming Duren's deal gets done before camp, Ausar Thompson's contract is next on the docket. -- Vincent Goodwill

Read the full Pistons offseason recap/season preview

Indiana Pacers: Sept. 11
Key additions: Kelly Oubre Jr., Larry Nance Jr.

Key retentions: None

Key subtractions: C Micah Potter

The Pacers didn't make any major offseason changes, but they will have two major additions to the roster they were missing last year: starting center Ivica Zubac, who was acquired at the trade deadline from the Clippers, and star guard Tyrese Haliburton, returning from injury for the first time since the 2025 NBA Finals.

Haliburton's presence lifted the Pacers into an Eastern Conference contender in 2024 and '25, and 16 months after a torn Achilles, they'll be counting on him to do the same in 2027. And Zubac will provide a different kind of center than Myles Turner provided the last time Haliburton was on the court. -- Jamal Collier

Read the full offseason recap/season preview

Southeast Division

Miami Heat: Aug. 31
Key additions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., Nick Richards

Key retentions: Andrew Wiggins, Simone Fontecchio

Key subtractions: Tyler Herro, Norman Powell, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis

Heat president Pat Riley landed the superstar he'd been searching for since LeBron James left Miami in 2016. Antetokounmpo is in the fold, and Miami is ready to contend for another title with the two-time MVP. Antetokounmpo is just as motivated to win his second title and remind everyone that he can be the best player in the league.

In the trade, the Heat gave up key players such as Herro, Ware and Jaquez and did not bring back Powell in free agency. They landed Thompson to a two-year, $13 million deal after the four-time champion sharpshooter worked out a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks. Miami also added Portis and Hardaway, but the team is still looking to bolster the roster around Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Heat offseason recap/season preview

Washington Wizards: Sept. 1
Key additions: AJ Dybantsa, Khris Middleton, Deandre Ayton, Tre Mann

Key subtractions: Cam Whitmore, D'Angelo Russell, Jaden Hardy

Key retentions: Trae Young

The Wizards got their jump on this pivotal offseason by acquiring Trae Young and Anthony Davis last season in trades.

Those were their two big moves and then came the big prize for losing 65 games last season - winning the lottery and drafting AJ Dybantsa with the first overall pick.

Ready to start winning games this season after losing 60 or more games in each of the past three years, Washington gave Young a four-year, $212 million contract. The Wizards added veterans like Khris Middleton and Deandre Ayton to bolster the depth behind their young core featuring the likes of Dybantsa, Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George, Tre Johnson and Will Riley. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Wizards offseason recap/season preview

Charlotte Hornets: Sept. 2
Key additions: F Naz Reid, G Grayson Allen, G Dennis Schroder, F Royce O'Neale, F Dorian Finney-Smith

Key retentions: G Coby White

Key subtractions: G LaMelo Ball, F Miles Bridges, G Josh Green, G Tre Mann

After enjoying their best season in a decade, the Hornets sharply changed course with the surprising decision to trade Ball, their franchise guard, to the Timberwolves.

Given that Ball was a borderline All-Star on a max contract, Charlotte opted for a "Moneyball" approach in hopes of avoiding the perpetual mediocrity that tripped up Trae Young's Atlanta Hawks in the recent past.

With Ball and starting forward Miles Bridges moved in separate deals aimed at collecting future draft assets and improving its cap flexibility, Charlotte is now the only team that doesn't have a single player on the books for at least $25 million next season. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Hornets offseason recap/season preview

Atlanta Hawks: Sept. 3
Key additions: Luguentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins, Kingston Flemings, Devin Carter, Ryan Nembhard, Zuby Ejiofor, Henri Veesaar

Key retentions: CJ McCollum, Jock Landale

Key subtractions: Zaccharie Risacher, Jonathan Kuminga, Gabe Vincent, Keaton Wallace

Atlanta continued to move forward from the Trae Young trade last season by being opportunistic this offseason.

The Hawks acquired Dort and Wiggins in separate trades from the Oklahoma City Thunder to add more help around emerging star Jalen Johnson. The Hawks also kept McCollum on a one-year, $21 million deal and drafted Flemings eighth overall.

Atlanta is loaded with young wings looking to take a step forward under Quin Snyder like Nickeil Alexander-Walker did last season in winning Most Improved Player. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Hawks offseason recap/season preview

Orlando Magic: Sept. 4
Key additions: C Nikola Vucevic, G Izaiyah Nelson

Key subtractions: F Moritz Wagner, G Jett Howard

Key retentions: F Jonathan Isaac, G Jevon Carter

The Magic's biggest move this offseason was hiring Sean Sweeney to replace Jamahl Mosley.

Orlando also brought Nikola Vucevic back on a one-year, $3.9 million deal since trading him in 2021 and will use his ability to score and shoot to space the floor for Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane.

The Magic blew a 3-1 lead over top-seeded Detroit in the first round of the playoffs after Wagner went down due to injury and were in desperate need of someone who can get easier baskets and make outside shots. Vucevic should help. Moe Wagner departed for Brooklyn via free agency, separating Franz from his brother for the first time in his pro career. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Magic offseason recap/season preview

Pacific Division

Los Angeles Lakers: Aug. 24
Key additions: C Walker Kessler, F Sandro Mamukelashvili, G Quentin Grimes, G Collin Sexton, F Kevon Looney, F Matisse Thybulle, G Cameron Carr

Key retentions: G Austin Reaves

Key subtractions: F LeBron James, C Deandre Ayton, G Marcus Smart, F Rui Hachimura, G Luke Kennard, C Jaxson Hayes

James informed the Lakers he would not be returning for next season on June 30. Two days later, the team transformed the roster, with Doncic squarely as the focal point.

The biggest addition -- literally and figuratively -- is 7-foot-2 center Kessler, acquired in a sign-and-trade deal with the Utah Jazz. L.A. sent two unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and pick swaps in 2028 and 2030, not to mention a four-year, $130 million contract, to acquire him.

Mamukelashvili, Grimes, Sexton, Looney and Thybulle also signed with the Lakers, and free agent Ziaire Williams and first-round pick Carr bolster the team's young prospect pool of Adou Thiero, Bronny James and Dalton Knecht.

The most important move, though, came when Reaves, coming off a career season in which he averaged 23.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game, signed a four-year, $180 million extension.

When the dust settled, it was a dramatic roster overhaul in what could prove to be one of the most consequential summers in franchise history, with the team also being sold for the second time in 14 months, this time to venture capitalist Josh Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger, who bought the Lakers from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Lakers offseason recap/season preview

LA Clippers: Aug. 25
Key additions: Rui Hachimura, Keaton Wagler, Brandon Ingram (TBD), Gradey Dick (TBD)

Key retentions: Kobe Sanders, Bradley Beal

Key subtractions: Kawhi Leonard (TBD), Nicolas Batum, Bogdan Bogdanovic, John Collins

What started as a reconfiguration at the trade deadline -- acquiring Darius Garland from Cleveland for James Harden and Bennedict Mathurin from Indiana for Ivica Zubac -- turned into a complete overhaul this summer after the Clippers let Bogdan Bogdanovic, Nicolas Batum and John Collins walk.

Their biggest move, however, was trading Leonard to the Toronto Raptors for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and draft picks, but that deal is in limbo pending the investigation into alleged salary cap circumvention by the team relating to Leonard's Aspiration endorsement deal.

In the meantime, LA added Illinois guard Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the draft and signed Hachimura away from the crosstown Lakers with a two-year, $28 million deal. And in a surprise move, Bradley Beal -- after declining his $5.6 million contract option for next season in June to test free agency -- ended up re-signing on a two-year, $13.2 million deal in mid-August to stay with the Clippers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Clippers offseason recap/season preview

Golden State Warriors: Aug. 26
Key additions: Yaxel Lendeborg, Brandon Williams, Georges Niang

Key subtractions: Quinten Post, Pat Spencer

Key retentions: Draymond Green, Al Horford, Kristaps Porzingis, Gary Payton II, De'Anthony Melton

The Warriors opted for flexibility and stability over a larger shake-up around Curry. Their much-publicized recruitment of James never gained much traction.

They brought back their veteran frontcourt trio (Green, Horford, Porzingis), but kept them all on short-term maneuverable contracts. They opted for the fit of Melton over a pursuit of scoring guard Anfernee Simons. Their big addition is Lendeborg, the 23-year-old rookie wing who they will rely upon to be a high-minute, high-impact rotation player immediately.

In the bigger picture, they protected their draft pick cupboard and lined up their books to have an ocean of cap space as they peer a bit deeper into the future while their core ages. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Warriors offseason recap/season preview

Phoenix Suns: Aug. 27
Key additions: F Miles Bridges, F Koa Peat, G Luke Kennard

Key subtractions: G Grayson Allen, F Royce O'Neale

Key retentions: F Dillon Brooks, G Collin Gillespie, C Mark Williams, G Jordan Goodwin

Phoenix followed up its surprising season with a series of moves to mostly keep its team intact, with some adjustments around the margins.

The Suns re-signed Gillespie (four years, $48 million), Williams (three years, $38 million), Goodwin (three years, $19 million) and Brooks (three years, $73 million) to new deals and made a major splash by trading Allen and O'Neale to the Charlotte Hornets for Bridges. And despite not having a pick until No. 47 in the second round of the 2026 draft, Phoenix was able to acquire Arizona player Peat -- who averaged 14.1 points on 52.8% shooting as a freshman for the Wildcats and was key to their Final Four run. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Suns offseason recap/season preview

Sacramento Kings: Aug. 28
Key additions: G Darius Acuff Jr., F Alex Karaban, G Emanuel Sharp

Key subtractions: G DeMar DeRozan, G Russell Westbrook

Key retentions: F Precious Achiuwa

Perry, currently in the organization's power seat, is continuing a steady transition toward the younger core he has drafted. Arkansas guard and No. 7 pick Acuff is the spotlight name on a roster populated with six players in their first two NBA seasons.

But they still have notable high-minute holdovers from the past regime, including Murray, Malik Monk, LaVine and Sabonis. Of those four, Murray appears the most locked-in as a stable member of the team's long-term vision. Perry explored trades for Monk, LaVine and Sabonis over the past year, but didn't value the proposed returns, and the three are expected to open the season in Sacramento. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Kings offseason recap/season preview

Northwest Division

Portland Trail Blazers: Aug. 17
Key additions: G Ja Morant, F Jeremy Sochan

Key retentions: C Robert Williams III

Key subtractions: F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, G Matisse Thybulle

Sadly, the Blazers made far more noise this offseason with their off-court business dealings than anything they did with their roster. New owner Tom Dundon's aggressive cost-cutting measures and ongoing fight for arena financing have distracted from the progress that Portland made on the court last season, when it reached the playoffs for the first time since 2021.

Although the Blazers were the only team that sat out June's draft by not making a pick, they will add two high-profile guards to a rotation that otherwise looks very similar to last season. Lillard, a franchise icon, is back from an Achilles tendon injury that sidelined him for the entire 2025-26 campaign, and Morant, a two-time All-Star, arrived in a trade that sent Grant and Murray to the Memphis Grizzlies. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Blazers offseason recap/season preview

Utah Jazz: Aug. 18
Key additions: G Darryn Peterson, C Jaxson Hayes, G Josh Okogie

Key retentions: C Jusuf Nurkic

Key subtractions: C Walker Kessler

The Jazz finally got some lottery luck, landing at No. 2 and taking Peterson, a gifted guard who has the potential to emerge as the face of the franchise. The hope was that Peterson would be the final major piece in Utah's rebuild, but that plan featured Kessler as the team's long-term starting center. Instead, the Jazz agreed to a sign-and-trade deal that sent Kessler to the Lakers in exchange for a pair of future first-round picks and two swaps.

The return was widely considered to be great value for Utah, particularly after Kessler's deal (four years, $130 million) pushed beyond the Jazz's comfort zone, but there is now a glaring need in the starting lineup alongside Jackson and Lauri Markkanen in the frontcourt. -- Tim MacMahon

Read the full Jazz offseason recap/season preview

Minnesota Timberwolves: Aug. 19
Key additions: G LaMelo Ball, G Josh Green, G Isaiah Evans

Key subtractions: F Julius Randle, C Naz Reid

Key retentions: G Ayo Dosunmu, G Bones Hyland, G Jaylen Clark

Wolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly continued to show his aggression, orchestrating a four-team trade with the Brooklyn Nets, Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets that sent out three-time All-Star Randle and the 2023-24 Sixth Man of the Year, Reid, and a future first-round pick to bring in the talented -- but polarizing -- Ball.

That move followed Connelly inking 6-foot-4 guard Dosunmu to a five-year, $112 million extension in June, following his acquisition at the deadline.

Minnesota also re-signed wing Clark and guard Hyland and acquired the 6-foot-6 Evans out of Duke with the No. 33 pick in the draft.

Coach Chris Finch also lost his top lieutenant on the bench, Micah Nori, who left to coach the Portland Trail Blazers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Timberwolves offseason recap/season preview

Oklahoma City Thunder: Aug. 20
Key additions: C Aday Mara, G Bennett Stirtz

Key retentions: G Kenrich Williams, C Isaiah Hartenstein

Key subtractions: G Isaiah Joe, G Aaron Wiggins, G Luguentz Dort

The extensions for both Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren triggered in July, leading to a trio of financially motivated trades to slash the tax bill and cost-control the current roster.

They sent Isaiah Joe to Detroit and traded Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort to Atlanta in separate moves, eroding their depth.

General manager Sam Presti made clear in an interview with The Oklahoman that the impression he's been given from ownership is "the savings generated this summer, and from being out of the tax the last several years, will be re-allocated to future teams."

That would mean extra breathing room to eventually extend core young players such as Cason Wallace and Ajay Mitchell. Wallace, the likely replacement starter for Dort, is extension eligible off his rookie contract into October. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Thunder offseason recap/season preview

Denver Nuggets: Aug. 21
Key additions: Marvin Bagley III, Lonnie Walker IV

Key retentions: Spencer Jones, Tyus Jones

Key subtractions: Watson, Tim Hardaway Jr., Jonas Valanciunas

Finding a resolution to Watson's restricted free agency was Denver's most important piece of summer business.

Watson is a draft success story, rising from the 30th overall pick into one of the league's more intriguing young two-way wings. But retaining the 23-year-old would have been expensive -- via either a sky-high luxury tax bill or a salary-slashing move to get off an important veteran and generate more breathing room for a new deal.

After Wednesday's deal to send Watson to Cleveland, Denver's front office can shift its attention to escaping the salary cap's second apron. The Nuggets are currently the league's only team above it. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Nuggets offseason recap/season preview

Southwest Division

Memphis Grizzlies: Aug. 14
Key additions: F Cameron Boozer, G D'Angelo Russell, F Isaiah Stewart, F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, C Quinten Post

Key retentions: None

Key subtractions: G Ja Morant, F Santi Aldama

Memphis finally traded Ja Morant, turning the last page from an ultimately disappointing chapter in franchise history, and already has his replacement as the face of the franchise in place: No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer. GM Zach Kleiman has overhauled the roster in the past few transaction cycles, acquiring four first-round picks when he traded Desmond Bane, a few more when he dealt Jaren Jackson Jr. and none for Morant, whose departure signaled a fresh start for the Grizzlies and him.

Memphis is in a full-blown youth movement, as 21-year-old forward GG Jackson is now the longest-tenured player on the roster. The Grizzlies say they believe they have a long-term foundation in place with their last few lottery picks: center Zach Edey, small forward Cedric Coward and power forward Boozer. -- Tim MacMahon

Read the full Grizzlies offseason recap/season preview

New Orleans Pelicans: Aug. 13
Key additions: None

Key retentions: C DeAndre Jordan

Key subtractions: F Kevon Looney

Despite capturing a combined 47 wins over the last two seasons under executive vice president Joe Dumars and general manager Troy Weaver, the Pelicans clearly believe that internal growth is the best path forward. Perhaps that justifies a near-silent summer in which the hiring of new coach Jamahl Mosley turned out to be the team's most notable move. Mosley becomes New Orleans' third coach since Dumars took the helm in April 2025. In addition to drafting Jaron Pierre Jr. in the second round, New Orleans signed just two new players over the summer in Kobe Bufkin and Hunter Dickinson, while bringing back 14 of the 15 players from last season's squad. -- Michael C. Wright

Read the full Pelicans offseason recap/season preview

Dallas Mavericks: Aug. 12
Key additions: F Morez Johnson Jr., F Zaccharie Risacher

Key retentions: Moussa Cisse

Key subtractions: Khris Middleton, Ryan Nembhard

The major changes made by the Mavericks this offseason were in the managerial and coaching ranks. After a seasonlong search, team governor Patrick Dumont hired Masai Ujiri to run the franchise's basketball operations, bringing the architect of the Toronto Raptors' 2019 title team to Dallas. Ujiri decided to part ways with coach Jason Kidd and recruited Dusty May, fresh off an NCAA title with Michigan, to replace him.

Johnson, who played for May at Michigan before the Mavs selected him with the No. 9 pick in the draft, is the headliner of the additions to the roster. Dallas added three potential immediate contributors in a six-team deal, acquiring former Grizzlies forward Santi Aldama, ex-Pistons guard Marcus Sasser and EuroLeague veteran Tarik Biberovic. The franchise also landed former No. 1 pick as part of the trade that sent Luguentz Dort from the Oklahoma City Thunder to the Atlanta Hawks. -- MacMahon

Read the full Mavericks offseason recap/season preview

Houston Rockets: Aug. 11
Key additions: G Marcus Smart, G Bogdan Bogdanovic

Key retentions: F Tari Eason

Key subtractions: F Dorian Finney-Smith, G Josh Okogie

After suffering a first-round postseason exit for the second consecutive season, the Rockets resisted the temptation to jump into the Giannis Antetokounmpo sweepstakes after adding former MVP Durant last summer. General manager Rafael Stone and coach Ime Udoka will instead lean on growth from the team's collection of young talent acquired in recent years, not to mention the continuity that comes with those players developing together over multiple seasons.

Houston signed Tari Eason to a five-year, $81.5 million extension over the summer. But outside of that, the Rockets focused on bolstering depth by bringing aboard veterans Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic. The club also brought in renowned shooting coach Chip Engelland from Oklahoma City. Engelland spent more than a decade with the San Antonio Spurs, winning two titles. -- Wright

Read the full Rockets offseason recap/season preview

San Antonio Spurs: Aug. 10
Key additions: F Tobias Harris

Key retentions: F Harrison Barnes

Key subtractions: None

San Antonio's surprising run to the NBA Finals never obscured its long-term vision for building a sustainable competitor around Victor Wembanyama. Clearly, the Frenchman views the future similarly, considering he signed a 25% max extension worth $252 million instead of the available 30% supermax escalators that would've rocketed the contract to $303 million.

Wembanyama did it to keep San Antonio's talented young core together for as long as possible, with added flexibility to acquire needed supporting players. The Spurs grabbed one of those in free agency in Harris, an experienced, reliable scorer who adds size (6-foot-8, 226 pounds) and physicality on defense while bolstering frontcourt depth in the draft. -- Wright

Read the full Spurs offseason recap/season preview
